extracted.intended_audience: journal editors, publishers, researchers and stakeholders interested in peer review models and open review practices
extracted.subtask_description: Summary of the BMC Group's implementation of open peer review: who knows reviewer identities, what is published with articles, procedural features (author response, decision type, coverage), and stated goals and evidence about effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Open peer review (BMC practice)
rubrics_metrics.description: In the open peer review process practiced by BMC, authors know who the reviewers are for all manuscripts during the peer review process, and if the manuscript is accepted for publication the named reviewer reports accompany the published article.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: First implemented in 2001 (BioMed Central). Intended to facilitate accountability and recognition, and to help train early career researchers about peer review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Goals and intentions: accountability and recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: The intention with open peer review is to make the reviewer (and the Editor) more accountable for peer review, and to provide recognition of the work that peer reviewers do.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Peer review is central to publishing integrity and discovery; BMC supports innovation in peer review and considers data from their implementation useful for learning about effectiveness and benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review requested by
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicates that the review process is initiated/requested by authors (as recorded in the BMC model summary).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer selected by
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMC's implementation allows selection of reviewers by journal editors, by an external service, or by the community, per-journal practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public interaction
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The BMC model summary indicates there is no public commenting/interaction as part of the review process for these journals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Author response
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors are able to respond to reviewer reports as part of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decision type
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions are recorded as a binary outcome (e.g., accept/reject) in the summarized policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review coverage
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer reports are expected to cover the complete manuscript (rather than, e.g., only abstracts or specific sections).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity known to (operational record)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational metadata indicates reviewer identities are known at least to editors or the review service managing the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer identity disclosure to authors
rubrics_metrics.description: Authors know who the reviewers are for all manuscripts during the peer review process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct from operational knowledge — BMC explicitly discloses reviewer identities to authors during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competing interests
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Competing interests / conflicts of interest are checked as part of the review workflow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: Open identities
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers' names are disclosed (open identities) as part of BMC's transparency measures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency: Open reports
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer reports are published alongside the article (named reviewer reports accompany the published article when accepted).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of outputs covered
rubrics_metrics.description: Journal accepted manuscripts; Other scholarly outputs
rubrics_metrics.guidance: BMC's open review practice applies to journal-accepted manuscripts and may extend to other scholarly outputs as noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Empirical findings on effects of open vs single-blind review
rubrics_metrics.description: Study (BMJ Open, 2015) findings: quality of peer review reports was slightly higher in BMC Infectious Diseases (open peer review) compared with BMC Microbiology (single-blind); no effect found in the Journal of Inflammation when it operated open vs single-blind review. Reviewer recommendations were similar in BMC Infectious Diseases and BMC Microbiology, but in the Journal of Inflammation reviewers were more likely to recommend acceptance under open review compared with single blind.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mixed evidence: small improvements in report quality in one comparison, no effect in another, and possible shifts in recommendation behavior in a third. Source: https://bmjopen.bmj.com/content/5/9/e008707
